item.title: Florida State coaching candidates after Mike Norvell fired: Who replaces him?
item.description: Florida State has moved on Mike Norvell, firing the embattled coach after a loss to Clemson dropped the Seminoles to 3-5 this year and 39-41 over Norvell’s seven seasons. Firing Norvell will require a $50.3 million buyout, one of the largest in FBS history. At a time when the athletics department is dealing with more than $400 million in debt, that financial outlay could impact the direction of the program’s next hire. The candidates to replace Norvell include a blend of offensive and defensive coaches, sitting Power Four head coaches and coordinators, and maybe even a blast from the past in former coach Jimbo Fisher . Toppmeyer: Brent Venables admits Oklahoma is 'embarrassing.' So was his contract extension Mendoza: Lincoln Riley was left for dead at USC. Then he stunned Ohio State At a minimum, the next hire will be expected to consistently place the Seminoles near the top of a topsy-turvy ACC and be in contention every year for the College Football Playoff, especially given the future expansion to a 24-team bracket . Here are the top candidates for the next FSU head coach: FSU football coaching candidates Manny Diaz, Duke About the only hangup on an otherwise strong résumé is Diaz’s three years at Miami from 2019-21, both because his teams underachieved and because, you know, Florida State hates the Hurricanes. But tossing Diaz aside for that reason would be beyond shortsighted; he graduated from Florida State and was an unpaid assistant under Mickey Andrews when the Seminoles beat Virginia Tech for the 1999 national championship. His most important work has come at Duke, which won nine games in 2024, another nine games and the ACC crown last season and is 6-2 heading into November after blowing out Boston College. Diaz should be seen as the early leader for the opening. Jimbo Fisher Fisher is hungry to get back into coaching and will push very hard to get his name in the mix for a second run with the Seminoles. His first was mostly terrific, highlighted by a national championship in 2013 behind what may be the best team in program history, but things fell apart near the end as Fisher eyeballed the exit. Likewise at Texas A&M, where things started well but rapidly deteriorated in his final season-plus. There are so many unanswered questions — such as what Fisher has learned off the sidelines, whether he has the energy to see a rebuild to fruition and even whether he has the chops to succeed in the current environment — that a reunion feels unlikely. Still, Fisher could be brought in at a discount and be given the checkbook to hire a crackerjack staff. item.title: Celtics Free-Throw Woes Vanish As Tatum Leads Top-5 Surge
item.description: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Everyone thought the Celtics would struggle to get to the line after trading Jaylen Brown. That fear was real, but the court has a different story to tell right now. The team has flipped a major weakness into a top-five strength in just five games. This sudden shift changes how Boston attacks defenses and controls the pace of play. According to Hardwood Houdini , the Celtics finished dead last in the NBA for free-throw attempts last season. They only got to the line 18.7 times per game. That stat looked like a curse after Brown, who generated 7.5 attempts per game, was traded for Paul George. George only took 3.4 shots from the stripe last year. The math said this roster would be passive. The results say otherwise. Tatum and Pritchard Change the Game Jayson Tatum is the engine driving this new aggressive style. His rate of reaching the line stands at 8.8 times per game, placing him third across the entire league. He even had a massive 22-attempt night against the Nets. That volume forces defenses to foul or risk letting him score at will. The team now shoots 28.8 free throws per game on average. That puts them fifth in the league, a huge jump from the basement. Payton Pritchard is also doing something he never did before. He averages four attempts per game when getting to the line. No prior season in his career saw him reach two attempts per game until now. Neemias Queta is up to five free-throw attempts per game this year. These numbers show that multiple players are attacking the rim with intent. The front office worried about losing Brown’s gravity. They forgot Tatum and Pritchard have their own gravity. Winning Streak Masks Small Sample Risks The Celtics hold a 4-1 record and have secured four consecutive victories. They beat the Bulls 125-111 on Friday night. The team dominated the paint despite the Bulls pulling down 20 offensive rebounds to Boston’s nine. Jalen Smith pulled down 12 boards while Neemias Queta and Mitchell Robinson combined for just 10. Robinson is now a team-worst, -26 on the season. He was the sole rotation player absent from the positives during the victory over the Bulls. Hardwood Houdini notes that the sample size is very small for these stats. The team hasn’t exactly been facing the stiffest competition either.

item.title: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympian Ciara Mageean after death at 34
item.description: A statement posted on Mageean's social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved ones [Getty Images] Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34. Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025. She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said. Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran . The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024. She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022. 'One of our own' Olympic legend Lady Mary Peters said Mageean was a "wonderful lady" who was "gracious, beautiful, talented and inspirational to the next generation". "We knew she was very ill and we knew that it was inevitable but we didn't expect it so soon," said the 1972 Olympic pentathlon gold medallist. Lady Mary's charity the Mary Peters Trust, which supports Northern Ireland athletes, had helped Mageean in her athletics career. "My charity supported her for as long as we could because she was so talented and we recognised that in her," said Last Mary. She said that Mageean had continued to inspire young athletes even while undergoing treatment for cancer and would be "sorely missed in the world of sport". Mageean won a gold medal at the 2024 European Championships in Rome [EPA] Sean Young, the secretary of Portaferry Gaelic Athletic Club, where Mageean played camogie in her younger years, said its members were in "disbelief and shock" at her death. He said Mageean had been a "fierce competitor" who began her sporting journey at the club before pursuing athletics. "Outside the sporting arena she is the most inspirational, humble person we have ever had within our club," he said. Obituary: Gifted athlete whose wit and smile left lasting impression Two-time Olympian Mageean dies aged 34 Down Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) said it was "honoured and privileged" to call Mageean one of its own, describing her as someone who never forgot her roots. "She touched the lives of so many people and she helped change the lives of so many," it said. "In her battle with illness she showed us courage, positivity and the value of life." Her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch, County Down, said it was "deeply saddened and heartbroken" by the death of its "cherished past pupil". "Ciara's kindness, strength, faith and unwavering determination were an inspiration to us all," it said. "She touched countless lives with her warmth, humility and generosity of spirit." item.description: Adric at Oracle Park, 2026 | Michael Elizondo / True Blue LA The 2026 season has come to a close with a flop that will likely only be remembered in Milwaukee. Locally, the 2026 NLCS will be seen as the end of an era, as cracks papered over for a couple of years finally burst open in a way that probably felt cathartic by proxy in Toronto and the Bronx. Today is not a day for that postmortem examination of what went wrong. Today we don’t cry that it’s over; we smile because it happened at all. No one is guaranteed a tomorrow, but one can look and wonder at the joys of yesterday. Although it never hurts to laugh at ourselves. View this post on Instagram Mild spoilers for Lanterns , but I was trying something new from a bit of the show that made me chuckle. On the anniversary of arguably the greatest game ever played, we return to that fateful night through the penultimate game of the regular season, when my mother wanted to visit Oracle Park for the first time. By Timely Ferry As someone who has lived in this part of the Bay Area for almost two years, after a year-long sabbatical near Fresno, I admit I don’t take as much public transit as I used to. But one way to get to Oracle Park I had always wanted to try was by ferry. A dedicated game-service ferry arrives about an hour before game time and leaves exactly twenty minutes after the last pitch for about $30 round trip. The selling point for this ferry is that it drops you off and returns from a port literally right by Oracle Park. There is regular service between Vallejo and San Francisco, but San Francisco’s ferry terminal is about a twenty-minute walk from Oracle Park. As for ferries, I have been on two in my life: a slow ferry that went from Belfast to Glasgow and back for a day trip I took after my job at The Parades Commission was essentially completed, where I had haggis for the first time (I liked it). Did I get up to any Catherine Breillat-esque shenanigans on the brief crossing? No, as it was too brief a crossing. Here, we have an hour-long ride where, if you arrive soon enough, you get a seat on calm water and the chance to buy snacks. Guess how I know about the exactly twenty minutes part? Yeah, we missed the return trip. For future reference, for best results with the special Vallejo ferry service, either try to leave the ballpark early or sit in the bleachers. But while head coach Charles Lee continues searching for consistent frontcourt flow, one major question lingers among fans and analysts: why is lottery pick Hannes Steinbach glued to the bench? Drafted 14th overall out of the University of Washington, Steinbach came to Charlotte as the nation’s leading college rebounder, averaging 18.5 points and 11.8 rebounds per game in his lone NCAA season. Steinbach proved that his production was no fluke during the Las Vegas Summer League , racking up double-doubles—including a pair of dominant 20-plus-point outings. Yet, through Charlotte’s opening stretch of the regular season, Steinbach has logged just 14 total minutes. Twelve of those came during a blowout loss to the Atlanta Hawks, and two came late in garbage time against the Washington Wizards. He also didn’t see the floor in Charlotte’s recent matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers. If the Hornets want to develop their lottery investment, this trend needs to change immediately. The Positional Lock and the Development Trap Lee’s hesitancy stems partly from how Charlotte views Steinbach’s position. While he showcased perimeter comfort and power-forward versatility in Europe (Würzburg Baskets) and in college, the coaching staff clearly views him primarily as a center. item.title: From Fleetwood embarrassment to 'magical' Anfield win 14 years in making
item.description: "Today has to be the day." That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating Liverpool thanks to Kai Havertz's first-half goal . Arteta was Arsenal captain the last time the Gunners won at Liverpool - 2-0 in 2012 - and they have had 16 unsuccessful trips in all competitions until Sunday's victory. The Spaniard's side, as they so often do, produced a defensive masterclass to keep out wave after wave of Liverpool attack to deliver a rare and historic win. Arsenal travelled to Anfield after an embarrassing loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Arteta said he thought that humbling loss in Lancashire could spur his side on to a historic win at Liverpool. "Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time," Arteta said after the game. "I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown. "Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it. "Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do." Before the match, centre-back Gabriel said that Arsenal were expecting a "big battle" and "big chaos" against Liverpool. That prediction was correct and, after going ahead, Arsenal were pinned back before the break. Although the second half was a bit calmer, they still defended resolutely and did not allow Liverpool a shot on target. The Gunners, who have kept six clean sheets this season, are now three points clear at the top of the table after nine games. Arsenal have kept six clean sheets in the Premier League this season [Getty Images] 'The togetherness we have is undefeated' Arsenal's 24 points is the most by any team after nine games of a season since the Gunners themselves in 2022-23. And only in the 2004-05 and 2007-08 seasons have Arsenal had more at this stage of a Premier League season. "It means a lot to our football club," match winner Havertz said after the win. "It's been 13 games [in the Premier League without a win here], its a crazy stat and it's what the fans deserve. We are happy we gave them that." The win was also the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet at Anfield in the Premier League since that victory in 2012. "That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do, this is what this stadium does to you," Declan Rice - who assisted Havertz's goal - added. item.title: 'Why does he have to complain?' - Virgil van Dijk fumes over Alexander Isak penalty snub as Liverpool lose to Arsenal
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Virgil van Dijk was left fuming after Liverpool were denied a first-half penalty for a shirt pull on Alexander Isak in their 1-0 defeat to Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday. The Dutchman questioned why a striker should need to protest with so many cameras on the pitch, after Kai Havertz's early strike proved enough to send the Gunners three points clear at the top. Van Dijk insists Isak penalty was clear Liverpool felt they should have had a spot-kick when Jurrien Timber held Isak's shirt as a cross flashed across the box, but neither referee Andy Madley nor VAR intervened. Speaking to Sky Sports, as reported by the Express, Van Dijk said: "I think it was a clear penalty. I've seen it back and I've seen it being given. Today it wasn't meant to be." Asked if Isak should have reacted more to convince the referee, Van Dijk replied: "We have 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras? Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal." Liverpool rue missed chances Van Dijk admitted Liverpool, who had Florian Wirtz hit the bar and Alexis Mac Allister head over a free chance before the break, could have done more in the final third: "Disappointed. We play at home, we had some opportunities. We tried everything. We could have done a bit better in the last 15 minutes to get more balls in the box." He continued: "It wasn't enough today and that's why disappointment is the feeling I'm having. When we conceded we played much better. Alexis could have changed the game." Iraola backs Van Dijk on penalty Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was equally adamant about the Isak incident: "It was a clear penalty. You hold the shirt, we can all see that he holds the shirt. The ball just goes one centimetre in front of Alex. Alex is going to hit the ball in front of the goal. The fact that you are even asking me that he should have gone to the floor, that's the thing. If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty for me. They call the penalty, 100 per cent." The Spaniard also pointed to the mistake from a goal kick that led to Havertz's winner: "We still have a lot of things to improve. I think we have things that I love in the team, in terms of the willingness and the spirit. I think there is something that I like in this team, but today we messed up a goal kick, we concede from there, things that we definitely need to improve." What's next for Liverpool? The defeat ended Liverpool's five-game winning run in all competitions, leaving Iraola with plenty to address before their next outing. The Reds must now regroup quickly, with a Champions League trip to Fenerbahce on Wednesday.

item.title: ‘He Needs To Be Fired,’ ‘Single-Handedly Ruined This Team’ — Ravens Fans Blame GM Eric DeCosta’s O-Line Decisions for Lamar Jackson’s Injury
item.description: ‘He Needs To Be Fired,’ ‘Single-Handedly Ruined This Team’ — Ravens Fans Blame GM Eric DeCosta’s O-Line Decisions for Lamar Jackson's Injury Lamar Jackson returned to lead the Baltimore Ravens’ offense Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, but his comeback lasted just one play. Jackson injured his right thumb on his first pass attempt and immediately headed to the locker room before being ruled out for the remainder of the game. The injury quickly turned attention toward Baltimore’s pass protection, with several fans blaming the offensive line for failing to keep Jackson clean. Much of that frustration was also directed at general manager Eric DeCosta, as Ravens fans questioned how the roster was constructed around their franchise quarterback. NFL World Blasts Ravens GM Over Offensive Line Moves Tyler Huntley, the Ravens’ backup quarterback, entered the game in Jackson’s place. But he, too, suffered an injury, forcing rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano to come in for several plays. One Ravens fan didn’t stay silent in her opinion about the Baltimore offensive line’s play. He spent eight seasons with the franchise before signing with the Arizona Diamondbacks in January 2026. Even after leaving, his value remains high given his track record. Arizona saw him post a 2.42 ERA across 67 outings, finishing 7-3 during 2026. That low ERA proves he can still get outs against tough lineups despite the change in scenery. The loss of Loáisiga is significant because he was a fixture in the Yankees’ late innings for nearly a decade. item.title: He's ready to sign, Star confirms new Liverpool owners could lead to deal
item.description: He's ready to sign, Star confirms new Liverpool owners could lead to deal One star has confirmed that Liverpool's new owners could hold the key to a deal. He's ready to sign on the dotted line. Liverpool have deals to get done over the next seven or eight months. Planning for their future beyond the 2027 transfer window is already underway and that means some enormous decisions must take place. Is Virgil van Dijk getting a new contract? What about Alisson Becker? Can the current batch of wingers work together? Is Giorgi Mamardashvili capable to taking the no.1 shirt? And that's just half of it. One major area of concern is the midfield, which doesn't look entirely 'right' this season - and was a struggle to get working last season, too. Liverpool will almost certainly address things next year, possibly in January, and that means deciding who stays as much as deciding who arrives. One player, in particular, faces a very uncertain future. New owners could change everything Alexis Mac Allister has been public about wanting a new contract at Liverpool. The club refused to offer him one in the summer, however, even while giving deals to Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai. Mac Allister made it clear that he does want a new deal with Liverpool, and that's something that feels a lot more likely thanks to his form this season. The Argentine has been one of the team's best players and quite unquestionably their best midfielder. Surely Liverpool would want to hand out a new deal to someone who Andoni Iraola has quickly come to depend on ? That just makes complete sense and if this current group in charge don't see that, perhaps the next lot will. Mac Allister spoke to Sky Sports about his contract situation and talked about the potential new ownership at Liverpool. 1892 Holdings now own a little over a third of the Reds and have the option to buy the club outright within the next 10 months. They could ultimately decide to give Mac Allister that new contract. Certainly, all previous decision making goes out the window. "There is a new ownership coming into the club,” said the player. “So everything can happen and we will see. Whether it is this season or next season, we will see what happens. “But right now I'm just enjoying my football, enjoying playing for this amazing club that is one of the best in the world. And we will see. We will see in the future what happens.”

item.title: Celtics Show They Can Score In Every Gear Against Bulls
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics proved on Friday night that they do not need just one way to win games. They crushed the Chicago Bulls 125-111 in their NBA Cup opener. This was not a fluke or a lucky night. The team showed it can score from the paint and from deep. Payton Pritchard led the charge with 30 points, but the real story was how the whole team moved the ball. NESN reported that Boston tallied 28 assists while shooting 51.2 percent from the field. That kind of balance is what makes them dangerous this season. The Scoring Mix Is Unstoppable Most teams rely on one star to carry the load, but Boston does not play like that. Jayson Tatum contributed 26 points alongside seven rebounds and seven assists. Paul George contributed 18 points and eight assists. The three leading scorers totaled 74 points, representing almost 60 percent of the team’s score. Boston also netted 56 points inside the paint while converting 10 three-pointers. This mix of inside power and outside shooting is what the Bulls could not handle. The bench players helped too, with Neemias Queta adding 13 points and Mitchell Robinson finishing with 11. Such depth enabled Boston to build an early lead and maintain it as Chicago attempted a comeback. A 32-point advantage was secured late in the second quarter. This margin provided starters sufficient rest to manage the remainder of the contest. Although the final difference was 14 points, the Celtics dominated for most of the evening. Yahoo Sports observed that Boston improved to 4-1 during the young season thanks to this victory. Securing the tournament’s opening match is promising, yet the true challenge lies ahead. Second Half Slump Needs Fixing There is one problem that Joe Mazzulla must fix before the next game. The Celtics looked serious for the first 24 minutes, then the Bulls started making things interesting. Chicago outscored Boston 62-47 in the second half, reducing a 32-point lead to 14 by the final buzzer. The Bulls made the game less comfortable after halftime. They won the second half by 15 points and reduced Boston’s final margin to 14. Those 18 points lost along the way might return to trouble them later. Four former patients who visited practice the day before signed the shooting shirts worn by the team, while players lined the court for the national anthem. A young fan displayed a sign stating, “Boston’s children saved my life.” The emotional moment was powerful, but the team needs to stay locked in for the full 48 minutes.
